t.E325.agn: Humans have consumed soured milk and fermented products containing lactic acid for centuries. In 1974 JECFA set the ADI for sodium lactate as 'not limited'. JECFA has reported that infants in their first three months have difficulty metabolising DL- and D(-)-lactic acid and has recommended that these forms not be used in infant foods.
t.E325.body: L(+)-lactate is a normal intermediate of mammalian metabolism and is largely converted to glycogen in the liver; the D(-) form is used more slowly.
t.E325.eff.0.w: Everyone except infants in their first three months
t.E325.eff.1.t: Infants in their first three months have difficulty metabolising DL- and D(-)-lactic acid; JECFA recommended that these forms not be used in infant foods
t.E325.eff.1.w: Infants in their first three months
t.E325.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E325.found.1: Cereal-based baby foods and complementary foods for infants (in the EU only for pH adjustment, L(+) form)
t.E325.prod: Obtained by neutralising lactic acid; lactic acid may be produced by fermentation or by chemical synthesis.
t.E325.pw.0: JECFA has recommended that D(-)- and DL-lactic acid not be used in infant foods; in the EU, only the L(+) form is permitted in infant formulae and complementary foods for infants.
t.E325.pw.1: It is a source of sodium. Sodium from additives is mostly lower than from salt.
t.E325.regx.0: ADI 'not limited'; the D(-) and DL forms should not be used in infant foods.
t.E325.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E325.regx.2: In complementary foods for infants, permitted only for pH adjustment and only in the L(+) form.
t.E325.summary: The sodium salt of lactic acid. In meat products it retains moisture, extends shelf life and regulates acidity.
t.E325.what: The sodium salt of lactic acid, used as an acidity regulator.
